name: Modes of Betrothal (Kinyanei Kiddushin)
notes: Specific discussion of the three modes of betrothal: money (kesef), document (shtar), and intercourse (biah), including minimum values and conditions

name: Betrothal by Money (Kiddushei Kesef)
notes: Betrothal effected through giving money or money's worth; dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel regarding minimum value (dinar vs. peruta)

name: Betrothal by Document (Kiddushei Shtar)
notes: Betrothal effected through a written document given to the woman

name: Betrothal by Intercourse (Kiddushei Biah)
notes: Betrothal effected through sexual intercourse; also the sole mode of levirate acquisition by the yavam

name: Conditional Betrothal (Kiddushin al Tenai)
notes: Betrothal made subject to fulfillment of a condition; rules on what constitutes a valid condition, including the requirement of doubled condition (tenai kaful)

name: Betrothal under Mistaken Assumption
notes: Betrothal where one party misrepresented their status or the item used; cases where betrothal is void due to material misrepresentation

name: Sivlonot (Pre-Marital Gifts)
notes: Gifts sent by a groom to a bride after betrothal; whether sivlonot sent after an invalid betrothal constitute a new act of betrothal

name: Betrothal through an Agent (Shaliach l'Kiddushin)
notes: Rules for appointing an agent to betroth on one's behalf; when agent exceeds instructions; competition between principal and agent betrothal

name: Betrothal with Forbidden Items
notes: Whether betrothal is effected using items from which benefit is prohibited (orlah, kilei hakerem, condemned ox, etc.) or items with special sanctity (terumah, maaser sheni, hekdesh)

name: Betrothal of Two Women Simultaneously
notes: Case where a man attempts to betroth two women simultaneously with one item worth a peruta, or betroths a woman and her daughter/sister together

name: Shetuki (Child of Unknown Father)
notes: Person who knows their mother but not their father; their status and marriage restrictions; distinct from foundling (asufi)

name: Asufi (Foundling)
notes: Child found in a public place who knows neither parent; their status and marriage restrictions compared to shetuki and mamzer

name: Gibeonite (Netinei)
notes: Descendants of the Gibeonites who converted in Joshua's time; their prohibited status with respect to marriage into the congregation (kahal)

name: Ten Categories of Lineage (Eser Yuchasin)
notes: The ten categories of those who ascended from Babylonia with Ezra (priests, Levites, Israelites, halalim, converts, freed slaves, mamzerim, Gibeonites, shetukim, asufim) and their permitted intermarriages

name: Lineage Investigation for Priestly Marriage
notes: How many generations back a priest must investigate a prospective bride's maternal and paternal lineage; presumptions based on public office or Temple service

name: Mitzvot Dependent on the Land (Mitzvot haTeluyot baAretz)
notes: Principle distinguishing mitzvot that apply only in Eretz Yisrael from those applying everywhere; exceptions such as orlah and kilayim that apply even outside the land

name: Women Exempt from Time-Bound Positive Commandments
hebrew: נשים פטורות ממצוות עשה שהזמן גרמן
notes: The rule that women are exempt from positive time-bound commandments and its exceptions; application in Kiddushin to distinguish men's and women's obligations

name: Father's Authority to Betroth His Minor Daughter
hebrew: רשות האב לקדש את בתו הקטנה
notes: The father's legal right to betroth his minor or young-adult daughter; limits of this authority and when it expires

name: Purification of Mamzer Status
notes: Rabbi Tarfon's view that mamzerim can be 'purified' over generations by marrying a Canaanite maidservant; dispute with Rabbi Eliezer

name: Credibility of Claims Regarding Betrothal
notes: Who is believed regarding claims of betrothal, its conditions, or the identity of the betrothed; disputed claims between parties and their legal effect on relatives

name: Betrothal with Priestly Portions
notes: Whether a priest who betroths a woman with his share of sacrificial offerings effects valid betrothal; distinction between most-holy and lesser-holy offerings

name: Choice of Vocation and Trade
notes: Rabbinic guidance on which trades to teach one's son; preference for Torah study over worldly vocation; ethical evaluation of various professions

name: Prohibited Seclusion — Specific Cases (Yichud)
notes: Specific rules: man may not be secluded with two women; woman may be with two men; exception when wife is present; seclusion with mother or daughter

name: Bachelor Prohibited from Teaching Children
notes: Prohibition on an unmarried man serving as a teacher of young children due to concern of improper conduct; parallel prohibition for women teachers

name: Double Condition Requirement (Tenai Kaful)
notes: Rabbi Meir's view that a legally valid condition must state both the positive and negative consequences; derived from the condition of Gad and Reuben (Numbers 32); dispute with Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel

name: Acquisition of Animals (Kinyan Behemah)
notes: Large animals acquired by passing reins/bit; small animals acquired by lifting or pulling; dispute between Rabbi Meir/Eliezer and Rabbis regarding pulling

name: Acquisition of Slaves (Kinyan Avadim)
notes: Modes of acquiring a Canaanite slave: money, document, or chazakah; how a slave acquires his own freedom; comparison with acquisition of land and movables

name: Barter Acquisition (Kinyan Chalifin/Chalipin)
notes: Acquisition through exchange of one item for another; once a party acquires what he receives, the risk for the item he gives transfers to the other party

name: Acquisition of Hekdesh by Speech
notes: The principle that consecration to the Temple treasury takes effect through speech alone, unlike acquisition between private parties which requires a formal act

name: Movable Property Acquired Together with Land (Agav Karka)
notes: Movable property can be transferred simultaneously with land through the act of acquisition performed on the land; also binds land to oath obligations of movables
